newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks end up in brisk trade, seen firm.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks end up in brisk trade, seen firm.

text.p: Argentine stocks gave back some gains at the close in heavy turnover Tuesday but traders expected the tone of the market to stay firm.

"The market is rubbing up against some resistance, which is logical considering how much it's gained recently," said Jose Napoli of traders Ignoto y Napoli. "But still it's the best of both worlds for us: a bullish international scenario and a domestic front with fading political worries."
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV tacked on 0.9 percent to close at 592.97, extending gains so far this month to 4.0 percent.

"The market got off to a good start thanks to the jump in Telefonica after it was upgraded by CS First Boston, which also pushed up Telecom and created a very favorable trading environment," said another dealer.
She said the bolsa then took its cue from the U.S. Treasuries market, "which rallied and drove the long bond yield down to 6.45 percent -- remarkably lower than our forecasts."
Traders said local private pension fund investments were likely to pick up towards the end of the week and should help keep the trend positive.
Floor volume swelled to 29.8 million pesos from 17.3 million Monday, while over-the-counter deals totaled 105.5 million pesos compared to Monday's puny tally of 21.7 million.

The broad market rose 0.7 percent, with risers beating decliners 43-19 and 20 stocks unchanged. Top main-tier gainers were pulp maker Celulosa, textile firm Alpargatas and cement firm Juan Minetti, up 4.0, 3.9 and 3.8 percent, respectively. Telefonica rose 2.1 percent and Telecom 1.3 percent.
Losers were led by construction stock Polledo and power utility Central Puerto, off 2.1 percent and 1.1 percent.
